consequence · the tc width sweep

tc512 was never a bad width. It was under-regularised for its width.

status · what is measured and what is not

The axis is monotone over 5× — and it stops at 0.01, because the 0.02 arm never started.

Eval LossRecon at ep 42 · mean of both sets · the only epoch all four arms share
1
0.02 produced no data. BSC:45106990 was cancelled 15 min after submission, still PENDING — elapsed 00:00:00, and no run directory exists on $SCRATCH. The optimum is unbracketed above 0.01.
2
The winner stopped at ep 67 of 100, still improving (0.0435 → 0.0416 over the last 12 epochs, rank still climbing). current.pth is on BSC $SCRATCH; a plain relaunch resumes.
3
Sigreg-on-sum is not a substitute. Catting z_a+z_b into the same pooled CF test at 0.005 gets ~40% of the gain of simply doubling the weight, and its Comp/Recon ratio (1.099) sits where its rank predicts — no composability win beyond the rank.
4
Single seed, one width. Whether tc256 and tc128 also want a bigger weight is untested — both already sit at rank 90–102, so headroom there looks smaller.
